summary: Analysis of 14 days of CGM and AAPS telemetry demonstrates exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), and a low Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Current basal rates, targets, CR, ISF, and DIA parameters are well-calibrated to baseline metabolic needs. Automated SMB and UAM features operate safely within configured safety limits without causing excessive IOB or late postprandial hypoglycemia. Declared meal strategies (prebolus timing, split boluses, and e-carbs) effectively manage postprandial excursions across both fast-carb weekday breakfasts and higher-fat weekend brunches.

analysis_steps.findings: Complete CGM data with 100% coverage (1,345 entries across 14 days) at a consistent 15-minute cadence. Telemetry and active AAPS profile structures are complete and fully authoritative.

Outstanding glycemic safety context with zero time below 70 mg/dL and minimal time above 180 mg/dL (0.3%). Glucose variability is low (CV 12.9%), reflecting minimal risk of severe hypoglycemia or severe hyperglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%, TAR 0.3%.

analysis_steps.findings: Basal rates effectively maintain fasting and overnight glucose within target boundaries (95-110 mg/dL overnight). Minor non-clinical drops to 70-71 mg/dL around 03:00 UTC on two nights do not warrant basal reduction given overall stability.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local average glucose ranges from 103.1 to 106.0 mg/dL between 00:00 and 04:00 local time.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios across all time segments return postprandial glucose smoothly to baseline within 3 to 4 hours. A DIA of 5.5 hours aligns well with observed insulin action and prevents insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: 240-minute postprandial glucose changes across recorded meals range between -11 mg/dL and +8 mg/dL.
data_gaps: Lack of isolated ISF correction boluses without carbs in telemetry; ISF validated indirectly via postprandial recovery.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both active and safely assist in damping postprandial peaks without causing late hypoglycemia. Delivery settings (3-min interval, 45-min max SMB basal) are appropriate.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled = true, uam_enabled = true, smb_interval_minutes = 3, max_smb_basal_minutes = 45.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are well-sized: Max Basal (2.4 U/h) is ~2.3x max profile basal rate, and Max IOB (8.0 U) safely accommodates largest meal boluses plus automated corrections. Dynamic ISF operates at 100%. Specific UI activation toggles in raw_settings are unpopulated in profile export.
data_gaps: UI switch toggles (e.g., smb_always_enabled, autosens_enabled) are null in the profile export payload.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal strategies match observed postprandial profiles. Weekday breakfast prebolus (20 min, 70% immediate) controls fast-carb absorption well, while weekend brunch (10 min prebolus, 60% immediate) manages higher-fat meals with minimal peak excursion.
analysis_steps.evidence: 28 carb entries totaling 1448g carbs and 142.2U insulin; 2-hour postprandial deltas average +33 to +57 mg/dL for breakfast and +62 to +70 mg/dL for brunch.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs configuration for weekend brunch (20g over 120 min) successfully models delayed absorption of fat/protein-rich meals, maintaining active COB to guide safe SMB/UAM micro-dosing. Carb impact floor (3 mg/dL/5 min) and max absorption (6h) are well calibrated.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch excursions resolve from a peak of 188 mg/dL at 120 min to 115 mg/dL at 240 min without late hypoglycemic overshoots; min_5m_carbimpact = 3, meal_max_absorption_hours = 6.0.

analysis_steps.findings: All profile parameters, AAPS safety settings, and meal strategy configurations are harmonious and working optimally. No parameter changes are required. Primary action is to maintain current settings and verify client UI toggles during routine reviews.
analysis_steps.evidence: 100% data coverage, 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV across 14 days of telemetry.

strengths: Excellent Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below Range over a 14-day period.
Very low glucose variability (CV 12.9%), indicating strong stability overnight and postprandially.
Basal rates and target segments effectively maintain baseline glucose near ~100-110 mg/dL.
Meal strategies (prebolus timing and e-carbs usage) are highly effective at preventing severe postprandial spikes or late hypoglycemia.
issues: Minor 2-hour postprandial excursions reaching up to 188 mg/dL during weekend brunches, though these resolve fully by 4 hours.
Some client-side AAPS UI toggle settings (e.g. Autosens switch status) are unpopulated in the Nightscout profile export payload.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Basal, CR, ISF, Target, and DIA Parameters
recommendations.description: Telemetry demonstrates optimal glycemic outcomes across all metrics (99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV). No changes to core profile parameters are indicated at this time.

recommendations.title: Verify Client-Side Activation Toggles in AAPS UI
recommendations.description: Core SMB and sensitivity limits are functioning effectively. Confirm in the AAPS app interface that Autosens and specific SMB activation conditions match intended preferences, as export payload raw settings contained null values.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain current profile parameters across basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA segments.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall glycemic control is exemplary (99.7% TIR, 0% TBR, 12.9% CV), proving that basal rates, carb ratios, sensitivity factors, and DIA are well-calibrated to daily metabolic needs.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate profile parameters after 14-30 days of data or if routine daily schedule changes significantly.

Morning fasting glucose is stable near target (90-105 mg/dL).
Midday basal rate maintains stability between meals without drift.
Evening basal holds baseline steady following dinner digestion.
Nighttime carb ratio segment is stable.
Morning CR (10 g/U) successfully returns post-breakfast glucose to baseline by 4 hours.
Midday CR (11 g/U) provides appropriate coverage for brunch and lunch entries.
Evening CR (9 g/U) brings post-dinner glucose smoothly to ~100 mg/dL.
Overnight sensitivity factor supports gentle automated loop corrections when needed.
Morning ISF functions well within dynamic loop calculations.
Midday ISF prevents over-correction during afternoon periods.
Evening ISF works safely with dinner boluses.
Overnight target range maintains high safety margin while preserving tight control.
Daytime target range provides an appropriate goal for automated basal and SMB adjustments.
Pre-bedtime target range helps avoid late evening dips.
5.5-hour duration of insulin action matches observed decay curves and prevents insulin stacking.
SMB and UAM are both enabled and effectively control postprandial rises without inducing low glucose.
Specific activation switches are unpopulated in raw profile settings export. Verify settings directly in the AAPS user interface.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: SMB delivery intervals and max basal minute caps provide timely corrections while limiting excessive micro-boluses.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max basal (2.4 U/h) and Max IOB (8 U) provide appropriate safety ceilings relative to max profile basal (1.05 U/h) and meal boluses.
Dynamic ISF factor is 100%. Explicit Autosens switches are null in export payload and should be verified in the app.
Carb absorption parameters accurately reflect digestion timing and prevent premature COB decay.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current meal strategy: use a 60-70% upfront bolus with 10-20 minute prebolusing for standard meals, and rely on active AAPS SMB/UAM micro-corrections for residual rises.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current carb ratios combined with a 5.5-hour DIA and active SMB/UAM achieve smooth postprandial glucose recovery to baseline within 4 hours without hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log explicit carb absorption notes when testing new or unusual meal compositions to verify if UAM alone manages unannounced carbohydrate rises.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 10-minute prebolus, 60% upfront bolus, and 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes with a 15-minute start offset.
exceptions.rationale: Higher fat/protein content causes delayed absorption. E-carbs keep COB active, enabling SMB/UAM to deliver safe automated coverage for lingering carbohydrate impact.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 20-minute prebolus, 70% upfront bolus, and no e-carbs.
exceptions.rationale: Rapid carbohydrate absorption requires a longer prebolus and higher upfront insulin share to suppress peak excursions without causing late drops.

implementation_steps: Review analysis findings and confirm that current glycemic metrics (99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR) meet clinical goals.
Verify AAPS client UI toggle settings (Autosens and SMB activation switches) directly in the app interface to ensure they align with export profiles.
Continue utilizing the declared prebolus timing (20 min breakfast, 10 min brunch) and e-carb strategies for mixed meals.
Monitor glucose trends routinely and re-evaluate if schedule, diet, or physical activity levels change significantly.
education: Time in Range (TIR) above 70% with Time Below Range (TBR) below 4% represents the standard international goal for automated insulin delivery systems. Achieving >99% TIR with 0% TBR indicates exceptionally well-tuned settings.

E-carbs (extended carbs) in AAPS simulate extended carbohydrate absorption in the mathematical model, keeping active COB elevated so the loop can deliver automated micro-boluses (SMB) as slow-digesting fat and protein convert into glucose.

DIA (Duration of Insulin Action) reflects how long rapid-acting insulin continues to lower blood glucose. Setting DIA accurately (e.g. 5.5 hours) prevents insulin stacking by ensuring the system correctly calculates remaining Active Insulin (IOB).
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
Never adjust multiple dependent parameters (e.g., Basal and CR simultaneously) at the same time. Always verify basal stability first before altering meal ratios.
Consult with your diabetes healthcare professional before making changes to your active insulin pump settings or closed-loop parameters.
